skill.name: spawn-terminal
skill.description: Open a separate terminal window for non-AI command-line tools after checking command help and options.
skill.summary: Runs user-requested CLI tools in a new terminal with a required help-check workflow.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The skill is designed to run user-selected CLI commands in a spawned terminal, so several external-command findings are valid risk indicators. Some Markdown backtick matches are scanner noise, but the cross-directory reference to ../agent/fork_terminal.py is a real filesystem boundary concern.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary external command execution is the core workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for the final command, show the exact command before launch, and refuse destructive or credential-handling commands unless the user clearly authorizes them.

remediation.issue: The skill references ../agent/fork_terminal.py outside its own directory.
remediation.suggestion: Package the helper inside the skill or expose it through a documented tool interface instead of requiring relative parent-directory access.

remediation.issue: The --help preflight still executes a user-selected binary.
remediation.suggestion: Treat the help check as command execution, validate the program name first, and avoid running untrusted local binaries.

content.user_title: Run CLI Commands in a New Terminal
content.value_statement: Developers often need long-running CLI tools without blocking their assistant session. This skill opens a new terminal, checks command help first, and then runs the requested non-AI command.
actual_capabilities: Identifies non-AI CLI command requests from the user.
Requires a --help check before running the final command.
Runs commands through a fork_terminal helper in a separate terminal.
Supports optional terminal output logging for debugging.
Supports blocking output capture when requested.
Directs AI-agent requests to a separate spawn:agent skill.
limitations: It depends on an external fork_terminal helper outside the skill directory.
It does not validate that a requested command is safe.
It is not intended to spawn Claude, Codex, or other AI agents.
The --help check can still execute untrusted local binaries.

use_cases.title: Run Build Commands
use_cases.description: Open a terminal for npm, Python, or other build tasks while keeping the assistant session available.

use_cases.title: Start Media Conversions
use_cases.description: Launch ffmpeg or similar tools in a separate terminal for long-running media work.

use_cases.title: Check CLI Diagnostics
use_cases.description: Run curl, package managers, or scripts after reviewing command help and options.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Simple Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a known CLI tool.
prompt_templates.prompt: Open a new terminal and run this non-AI command: npm run build.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Long Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep the assistant session free while a process runs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn a terminal for ffmpeg to convert video.mp4 into output.gif after checking the help options.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Debug Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Need terminal output saved for later review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run this Python script in a new terminal and log the full terminal output for debugging.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Before Running
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced command with options that should be checked first.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the command help for curl, then open a terminal for the final request I provide.

output_examples.input: Open a new terminal for npm run build.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks npm help, reviews the options, and launches the build command in a separate terminal.

output_examples.input: Run ffmpeg conversion and save debug output.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks ffmpeg help, starts the conversion in a new terminal, and returns the log file path.

output_examples.input: Capture output from a Python script.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks Python help, runs the script with capture enabled, and returns the completed terminal output.

best_practices: Review the exact command before the terminal is launched.
Use output logging for commands that may fail or run for a long time.
Use the separate spawn:agent workflow for Claude, Codex, or other AI agents.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for commands that delete, overwrite, or exfiltrate data without explicit approval.
Do not skip the help check when command syntax is unfamiliar.
Do not use this skill to start AI agents or coding assistants.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It opens a separate terminal and runs a non-AI command-line tool after checking command help.

faq.question: Does it run AI agents?
faq.answer: No. It directs Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and similar agent requests to a separate agent workflow.

faq.question: Why does it run --help first?
faq.answer: The help check reduces syntax mistakes and makes command options visible before the final launch.

faq.question: Can it capture output?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes optional capture and logging modes through the terminal helper.

faq.question: Is every command safe to run?
faq.answer: No. Users should review commands carefully, especially destructive commands or commands that handle secrets.

faq.question: What tools can it launch?
faq.answer: It can launch typical CLI tools such as npm, ffmpeg, curl, and Python when the local environment supports them.
